textbookBox.concept: We begin with Amma's rangoli. It is made by joining dots, and when we join them we get shapes that we can name. In the rangoli we see shapes such as a square, a triangle and a circle.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.speakEn: We begin with Amma's rangoli. It is made by joining dots, and when we join them we get shapes that we can name. In the rangoli we see shapes such as a square, a triangle and a circle.

beats.en: Collect a cardboard box and open it out carefully. Every flat part of the box is called a face, and when the box is opened we see the faces as flat shapes. Most of them are rectangles, and some may be squares.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 3 maths · Fun with Shapes · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 corners. We can build one by joining four sticks. In a rectangle the opposite sides are equal in length. This does not mean all four sides must be equal.

beats.en: A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 corners. We can build one by joining four sticks. In a rectangle the opposite sides are equal in length. This does not mean all four sides must be equal.
beats.speakEn: A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 corners. We can build one by joining four sticks. In a rectangle the opposite sides are equal in length. This does not mean all four sides must be equal.

beats.en: Chess boards, ludo boards and floor tiles are square in shape. If we fold a square tile in half it becomes a rectangle, so the two shapes are close relatives. Both a square and a rectangle have 4 sides and 4 corners.
beats.speakEn: Chess boards, ludo boards and floor tiles are square in shape. If we fold a square tile in half it becomes a rectangle, so the two shapes are close relatives. Both a square and a rectangle have 4 sides and 4 corners.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 3 maths · Fun with Shapes · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: Look at the corner of a tile, a table or a maths book. Such a corner is called a square corner. To check a corner, pile one square over another, or one rectangle over another.
